title: Select Sector indices — conditional quarter-end secondary reweighting (24%/4.8%/50% breach test)
source: EST: rule-derived, not a scheduled publication. SEC EDGAR, Select Sector SPDR Trust Form 497, accession 0001193125-26-031948, document d85739d497.htm, RE-FETCHED DIRECT 2026-09-06 by this session (HTTP 200, 2,388,335 bytes) and re-parsed rather than inherited from the March sibling, because a rule quoted second-hand is a rule nobody checked. It reads verbatim: "Additionally, if, on the second to last business day of March, June, September, or December a company has a weight greater than 24% or the sum of the companies with weights greater than 4.8% exceeds 50%, a secondary reweighting will be triggered with the reweighting effective date being after the close of the last business day of the month." June 2027's last business day is Wednesday 2027-06-30 and the second-to-last is Tuesday 2027-06-29 (both weekdays verified this session, no US market holiday falls between), so the test is 06-29 and the trade, IF triggered, clears at the 06-30 close. The same filing dates the PRIMARY June rebalance to "the closing prices of the second Friday" effective "after the market close on the third Friday" -- 2027-06-11 and 2027-06-18 -- but NYSE is closed Friday 2027-06-18 for Juneteenth (juneteenth-market-closure-2027-06-18, already tracked), which pulls the effective date to Thursday 2027-06-17, the displacement the sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-03-31 entry already recorded. Filed estimate because the trigger is CONDITIONAL -- most quarters it does not fire, and no primary source can pre-confirm that it will. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the fomc-minutes-2027-06-30 initial research (2026-09-06) and proposed because it lands on that event's OWN DATE, which is the point: the +/-5-day corridor around 2027-06-30 held exactly one tracked entry before this proposal (consumer-confidence-2027-06-29), and what the corridor was missing is that 2027-06-30 is a quarter-end close carrying a conditional forced index trade. That matters to the minutes ledger's central claim rather than being bookkeeping. That ledger measured, across all 160 FOMC minutes releases 2007-2026, that a minutes day is statistically an ORDINARY session (0.776% mean |S&P| vs a 0.798% baseline, bootstrap p=0.40) and that the dead-week venue its 12-30 sibling called 'the most amplification-friendly venue a minutes release ever gets' actually runs 0.676x trailing-60d median volume while June quarter-end runs 1.149x. So the one session where a minutes release could plausibly be amplified by flow is exactly this one, and this entry is the flow. THE BASE CASE IS THAT IT DOES NOT FIRE, and that is registered rather than asserted: a 06-29 trigger requires a limit breach to RE-OPEN in the seven trading sessions after the 2027-06-17 rebalance re-caps everything, which is unlikely straight out of a reset -- the same reasoning the March sibling filed as a backstop, registered here as FT-fomc-minutes-2027-06-30-3, score by 2027-07-01. Honest caveats inherited and re-stated rather than laundered: the March entry's breach evidence came from State Street's daily ETF holdings files (capped index weights drifted by price plus a cash residual), which are floors on the float-adjusted index weights the test actually applies to, and the filing's step-2 wording admits two readings whose implied trade sizes differ by roughly 8x -- a fork already registered as FT-sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-03-12-1. Low impact and estimate status: it widens caution about the 2027-06-29 and 2027-06-30 closes and licenses nothing, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4/G1) is index-flow-keyed. Kind `sector` is the closest fit the enum offers for a market-structure flow event; the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane.
